method.label: Use the bisector and triangle inequalities

annotationRationale: The angle bisector theorem expresses BC in terms of AC. Triangle feasibility then becomes a system of quadratic inequalities determining the exact interval.
sourceMethod: Followed the official angle-bisector and three-triangle-inequalities solution, including its completing-square calculation. Added an explicit feasibility argument for every value in the resulting interval.

review.mathCheck: The bisector theorem gives BD=30/q for q=AC>0. The three triangle inequalities reduce to an always-positive quadratic, q<15, and q>3. Conversely, every q in (3,15) produces a triangle whose bisector gives CD=(3+30/q)q/(10+q)=3. The endpoints are degenerate and excluded, so m+n=18, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA solution 12 on pages 6–7, including the same three inequalities and completing-square check. The supplied figure confirms q=AC, r=BD, and CD=3. The candidate adds a correct sufficiency argument.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed bisector ratio and triangle feasibility, with quadratic inequalities as support, accurately describe the method. No discriminant concept is needed.
